terms.gloss: secretly; as a preposition, without the knowledge of
terms.grammar: adverb; preposition with the ablative or accusative
evidence: Caes. BC 2.32: nōn sibi clam vōbīs salūtem fugā petīvit? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Without someone’s knowledge: clam vōbīs (Traupman), clam patrem.

evidence: Liv. 21.63.9: sine līctōribus profectum clam fūrtim (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: secretly, on the quiet, on the sly
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 523: clanculum abiī ā legiōne
Ter. Heaut. 472: illōs ibi esse et id agere inter sē clanculum
terms.comment: A diminutive of clam; Lewis & Short calls it ante-classical but frequent.

evidence: Cic. Agr. 1.1: ea nunc occultē cunīculīs oppugnātur (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ad. 3.2.30: neque id occultē fert (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: clanculum abiī ā legiōne: operam hanc subrupuī tibi
phrases.english: I slipped away from the army on the quiet: I stole this time for you
it is now being attacked in secret, by mines

sources: Lewis & Short: clam · Lewis & Short: clanculum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 337.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
